newsitem.title: USA: U.S. barley growers stop short of seeking EEP subs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. barley growers stop short of seeking EEP subs.

text.p: Activation of the U.S. Agriculture Department's dormant export subsidy program may not provide U.S. barley producers with relief from depressed prices, the head of the National Barley Growers Association said on Monday.

Although the USDA has said it might start subsidizing barley malt exports through its Export Enhancement Program, a similar subsidy for barley could backfire, Herb Karst, head of the barley growers group, said.

"A subsidy could invite more imports from Canada," Karst said in an interview after addressing the U.S. Feed Grains Council meeting. "And if the USDA did reactive the export subsidy program, are we going to get any benefits back to our producers?"

U.S. barley producers, mostly based in the Dakotas, Minnesota and Montana, compete with Canadian farmers across the border. But some industry experts have forecast that Canada will need to import barley to meet its own needs in a few years.
